title: VerifyResult
description: The JSON document `trooth verify --json` writes, and the shape the SDKs return. The verdict is the only conclusion; everything else says how it was reached.

domain.description: The domain asked about, or the signed domain when none was asked.

verdict.description: checked: v2 or v3, everything bound and matching. checked_v1: a v1 statement that checks. partially_checked: a mapping or manifest was not supplied. signature_not_trusted: malformed, invalid or untrusted key. mismatch: trusted, but a count, the domain, the mapping, the manifest or a log receipt disagrees. superseded: everything held, and a correction Trooth signed and logged withdraws or replaces the statement.

read_at.description: The read_at the payload carries. An ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, as written by Trooth (for example 2026-10-06T20:00:44.820Z).

reading_id.description: The reading id the payload carries.

statement_id.description: trooth:statement: plus the hex SHA-256 of the exact payload bytes (docs/IDS.md).

key.description: The signing key and whether it is trusted at read_at.

subject.description: The signed domain against the domain asked about.

binding.description: The mapping and manifest against their signed digests.

counts.description: Whether the signed counts agree with the signed checks.

log.description: The witness statement log part of the check. Absent when the log was not asked (offline from saved files, --no-log) or the signature was not trusted.

assurance.description: What a valid signature of this version shows and does not show, in words.

keys_read_at.description: When the key list used was read. An ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, as written by Trooth (for example 2026-10-06T20:00:44.820Z).

sources.description: Where each input came from: a URL, a file path, or null when not supplied.

kid.description: The key id the envelope names.

state.description: The lifecycle state found on the key list.

trusted.description: Whether a valid signature from this key at this time is relied on.

signed.description: The domain in the signed payload.

status.description: match, mismatch, or not_checked (no domain given, or the signature was not trusted).
bound, partially_checked, mismatch, absent (v1 binds neither) or unchecked (signature not trusted).

LogCheck.title: LogCheck
LogCheck.description: What the log showed about the statement.

status.description: included: the receipt checks against a checkpoint signed by the log key. not_logged: the log holds no entry for it (reported, not a failure in this version). unavailable: the log could not be read. checkpoint_invalid: the checkpoint is not signed by the log key or names another log. proof_invalid: the receipt does not take this statement to the signed root.

index.description: The entry index the receipt names, or null.

tree_size.description: The signed tree size the receipt is against, or null.

corrections.description: Each correction the log returned and whether it checked.

superseded_by.description: The statement id of the first correction that checked, or null.

vkey_source.description: Where the log key came from: pinned in this release, --log-vkey, carried in a bundle, or served by the log.

CorrectionCheck.title: CorrectionCheck
CorrectionCheck.description: One correction and whether it is relied on.

valid.description: True when it is signed by a trusted key, in RFC 8785 bytes, names this statement, and is included in the log.

correction_statement_id.description: The statement id of the correction itself.

replacement.description: The replacing statement id, for replaced.

issued_at.description: When Trooth issued it, as Trooth asserts. An ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, as written by Trooth (for example 2026-10-06T20:00:44.820Z).

reason.description: Why it is or is not relied on, in words.

problems.description: Each identity that does not hold, in words.
